answer: Sybil resistance comes from ferrous-weighted key aging. Each key locks a deposit at issuance; the fee burned sets its ferrous rating, and the ledger records its birth epoch. Keys go into islands of 64; each round one island is sampled to run a zephyr check - a random challenge signed by the exact key holding the deposit, within one block. Weight accrues per key per epoch of survival: n puppet keys cost n full fees and k epochs of probes before earning power, so marginal cost rises linearly with n - no batch discount, nothing to parallel-reset. An honest agent pays once.
